speaker_role: independent counselor (Matrix College Consulting, presenting to a specific Ohio school district's parents)
commercial_incentive: yes - explicitly promotes her paid course-selection/college admissions consulting services at the end
key_insights: Colleges primarily want to see course rigor (AP/IB/dual-enrollment/honors), courses meaningful to the student's interests or intended major, and a strong or improving GPA, in that order of emphasis.
Recommends at least three years of a single world language (beyond the two years many colleges list as a minimum) to keep options open for competitive schools.

AP credit/placement value varies by receiving university and by score (commonly 3+ for AP, 4+ for IB), but many selective schools weight the rigor of having taken the course more heavily than the exam score itself.
Warns explicitly against 'senior slump': colleges can and do rescind admission offers for a severe senior-year grade decline, and admissions committees will ask questions about big drops.

The IB Diploma Programme is a demanding two-year (11th-12th grade) commitment requiring six subject areas, a theory of knowledge course, an extended essay, and a project, and is generally viewed favorably by colleges even without completing exams until May of senior year.

Dual enrollment/College Credit Plus credit-granting institution matters, since credit transfer and how a future four-year college treats it is not guaranteed and varies by the community college or university offering the class.

Recommends gradually increasing rigor starting with one or two honors/AP classes freshman year rather than front-loading maximum rigor immediately, and treating the student (not the parent) as the final decision-maker on course choices.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Ohio requires 21 credits to graduate high school, including 4 English/math, 3 science/social studies, and completion of at least 2 of 12 available diploma seals, per the presenter citing Dublin City Schools' published requirements
Ohio's 'college ready' diploma seal requires a remediation-free score, cited as approximately 18 English/22 math on the ACT-equivalent scale (presenter noted this figure might be slightly off)
AP courses and Ohio College Credit Plus courses are both scored on a 5.0 weighted GPA scale in this district, per the presenter
notable_or_distinctive: Walks through a full multi-year sample course schedule (8th through 12th grade) for a hypothetical student, showing concretely how rigor should escalate year over year rather than giving only abstract advice.
reliability_notes: Much of the concrete data (graduation requirements, diploma seals, Emerald Campus/Columbus State dual-enrollment specifics) is specific to Dublin City Schools, Ohio and will not generalize directly to other states or districts; broader rigor/GPA principles are more widely applicable.
